newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen adding reserves via 3-day system rp's.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen adding reserves via 3-day system rp's.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Monday through three-day system repurchase agreements, analysts said.
"The firm Federal funds rate is telling us that they have a shortage of reserves so we think they'll do three-day system rps," said Michael Moran, chief economist at Daiwa Securities America Inc.
At 1055 EDT/1455 GMT, Fed funds were trading at 5-1/2 percent, above the Fed's 5-1/4 percent target for the rate.
"We (calculate) an add need of about $4.0 billion per day," said Moran.
"They already have in place a 7-day operation from Thursday but we don't think that's going to be enough to keep pace with reserve needs," Moran said.
Kim Rupert, senior economist at MMS International, is expecting the Fed to add reserves through three-day or overnight system repurchase agreements.
"They still have an add need left," said Rupert, referring to the Fed, "And there's pressure on the funds rate from the tax date today."
